# mlr3hf <img src="man/figures/logo.png" align="right" width = "120" />

Package website: [release](https://mlr-org.github.io/mlr3hf/) | [dev](https://mlr-org.r-universe.dev/mlr3hf)

Integration of [Hugging Face](https://huggingface.co) datasets with the
[`mlr3`](https://mlr3.mlr-org.com/) ecosystem.

<!-- badges: start -->
[![R-CMD-check](https://github.com/mlr-org/mlr3hf/actions/workflows/R-CMD-check.yaml/badge.svg)](https://github.com/mlr-org/mlr3hf/actions/workflows/R-CMD-check.yaml)
<!-- badges: end -->

## What is `mlr3hf`?

[Hugging Face](https://huggingface.co/) provides a large collection of datasets
for machine learning and data science. `mlr3hf` connects these datasets with
the [`mlr3`](https://mlr3.mlr-org.com/) ecosystem.

Datasets can be downloaded from Hugging Face and converted into `mlr3` data
backends and tasks.

`mlr3hf` supports both Parquet datasets generated by Hugging Face and the
original dataset files stored in a repository.

## Installation

Install the last release from CRAN:

```{r eval = FALSE}
install.packages("mlr3hf")
```

Install the development version from GitHub:

```{r eval = FALSE}
pak::pak("mlr-org/mlr3hf")
```

## Example

### Loading a Hugging Face dataset

`hfdt()` creates an `HFData` object representing a Hugging Face dataset.
The object provides access to the dataset and its metadata and can be
converted into an `mlr3::Task`.

```{r}
hf_data = hfdt(
  repo_id = "scikit-learn/iris",
  config = "default",
  target = "Species",
  task_type = "classif"
)

hf_data
```

### Creating an `mlr3` Task

The `HFData` object can be converted into an `mlr3::Task`.

```{r}
task = as_task(hf_data)
task
```

### Basic train + predict

The resulting task can be used with the `mlr3` ecosystem in the same way as
other `mlr3` tasks.

```{r}
learner = lrn("classif.rpart")

split = partition(task, ratio = 0.67)

learner$train(task, split$train_set)

prediction = learner$predict(task, split$test_set)

prediction$score(msr("classif.acc"))
```

### Resample

The task can also be used directly with `mlr3` resampling strategies.

```{r}
resampling = rsmp("cv", folds = 3L)

rr = resample(task, learner, resampling)

rr$aggregate()
```

### Direct task construction

For workflows where the intermediate `HFData` object is not required,
`tsk()` can be used to construct an `mlr3::Task` directly.

```{r}
task = tsk(
  "hf",
  repo_id = "scikit-learn/iris",
  config = "default",
  target = "Species",
  task_type = "classif"
)

task
```

## Documentation

The [package documentation](https://mlr-org.github.io/mlr3hf/) contains the complete
documentation and examples for `mlr3hf`.

For more information about the `mlr3` ecosystem, see the
[`mlr3` book](https://mlr3book.mlr-org.com/).


## Extension Packages

`mlr3hf` is part of the `mlr3` ecosystem and can be used together with
the many extension packages available for `mlr3`.

For example, `mlr3learners` provides learners that can be used with tasks
created by `mlr3hf`.

See the [mlr3 ecosystem](https://mlr-org.com/ecosystem.html) for a complete
list of extension packages.


## Contributing to `mlr3hf`

`mlr3hf` is a free and open source software.

If you encounter problems using the package, find missing or misleading
documentation, or want to suggest a feature, please open an issue in the
[issue tracker](https://github.com/mlr-org/mlr3hf/issues).

Pull requests are welcome and will be included at the discretion of the
maintainers.

Please consult the [mlr3 wiki](https://github.com/mlr-org/mlr3/wiki/) for
development and contribution guidelines.
